title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026
summary: Nvidia took the wraps off its Rubin HPC GPU at Supercomputing 2026. This new GPU will give scientists, engineers, and analysts over 50,000 CUDA cores to speed up agentic HPC workloads when it arrives in 2028.
body: The Supercomputing 2026 conference is under way, and despite continuing turmoil elsewhere in the company, Nvidia has lots to reveal at the show. Foremost among its announcements today, Nvidia took the wraps off a new member of the Rubin GPU family called Rubin HPC , a chip that the company says is meant to accelerate agentic workflows and simulation for scientists, engineers, and analysts working with large data sets. To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C. Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip's physical layout alongside the announcement. (The representative image shared by the company wouldn't appear to take this into account.) To keep data moving between Rubin HPC GPUs, Nvidia will use its NVLink 7 interconnect. The company didn't share any new details of the bandw…

title: Hacker gets Doom running on a USB flash drive's built-in LCD, played by copying files
summary: Aaron Christophel ported Doom to the LCD on a MOVESPEED MSSU10 flash drive and controls it with file transfers.
body: Doom now runs on a USB flash drive ’s built-in LCD and is played by copying files to and from it, as hardware hacker Aaron Christophel showed in a teardown video . The marking on the drive’s display chip had been removed, but an open debug port let him extract its firmware, which enabled identification. He was then able to use AI to reverse-engineer the hardware and get the game running on the drive’s screen. The off-the-shelf drive, the MOVESPEED MSSU10, has USB-A on one end and USB-C on the other, and the 128GB model, the smallest capacity in the range, cost him about 50 euros. Its screen normally shows status data such as transfer speed, how full the drive is, and its temperature. The main flash controller is the Silicon Motion SM2320G, one we have reviewed in portable SSDs like the Kingston XS2000 and Lexar SL660 Blaze , with a separate C*Core CCM4101 microcontroller — which has 2MB of flash and a small amount of RAM to itself — for the 428 x 142 color LCD. The NAND carries SanDisk markings. All of this is fairly standard portable SSD hardware, aside from the display. The drive’s metal body uses heavily glued plastic end pieces but, past that, the display lifts off first and u…

title: 3D printing dev’s free tool unlocks curved printing along all three axes

body: Alpaca Engineering posted a YouTube video yesterday showcasing his self-hostable non-planar slicer. He explains that most non-planar 3D printing — printing across all three axes, rather than in 2D horizontal layers — demonstrations are usually for research purposes, for demonstration and experimentation, with no easy way for most 3D printer owners to try out non-planar 3D printing. His project, named PancakeSlicer, aims to fix this by making his non-planar slicing algorithm as easy to implement as existing slicing workflows, even improving upon it with 3D printer management features. Alpaca Engineering explains that every few months, a non-planar 3D printing demonstration goes viral, but is rarely adopted practically by most 3D printer owners. Most non-planar experiments are for research, with half-abandoned GitHub projects. He further explains that non-planar isn’t widely adopted not because there aren’t any general-purpose non-planar slicers, but because it’s not accessible and easily implemented in a familiar workflow, with 3D printer owners spoiled by modern workflows and not needing to manually run G-code directly from an SD card. body: Update 11/16/2026 2:40pm PT: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has now clarified the nature of the failure in an interview on CNBC , saying the HPE routers were not at fault. title: Modified Ender 3 becomes a $450 bioprinter for 3D printing engineered living materials
summary: Microbiologists at the University of Rochester have modified an Ender 3 FDM printer into a 3D bioprinter for $450 and outperforming 3D bioprinters costing more than $100,000.
body: Microbiologists at the University of Rochester modified an Ender 3 FDM 3D printer into a 3D bioprinter for engineered living material (ELM) research. The team used SolidWorks to create the 3D model and sliced it in Slic3r, akin to a normal 3D printing workflow, with modified settings for the custom syringe pump print head. The $450 3D bioprinter makes ELM research more accessible, as bioprinters usually cost over $100,000. Synthetic biology is like combining engineering with microbiology, treating microbes as machines and physical building blocks to achieve various functions. In the journal ACS Applied Polymer Materials, biologist Anne S. Meyer et al. published a 3 D Bioprinting of Engineered Living Materials paper in August. The paper says that synthetic biology and 3D bioprinting have advanced ELM research, but the hardware costs and the inability of the expensive hardware to maintain the structure limit further progress. Hitting two birds with one stone, the researchers built an open-source, affordable 3D bioprinter from an Ender 3 and created their own support slurry, allowing the ELMs to keep their shape. body: It looks like AMD is trying to get back into the good graces of gamers, with its CEO, Dr. Lisa Su, joining the grand opening of Micro Center Austin. The company shared official photos of AMD’s chief executive cutting the ribbon to mark the store’s opening on its Instagram page, while a Redditor shared a short clip showing her making the rounds among the people waiting to get inside the shop and signing a Gigabyte Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU, one of the best gaming GPUs you can buy today. AMD CEO Lisa Su meeting and interacting with attendees today at the grand opening of the new Micro Center in Austin. from r/pcmasterrace AMD has been saying that it is a data-center-first company repeatedly since 2024. Dr. Su reiterated the stance in an interview earlier this month, at which point some in the press finally decided to notice. The reporting naturally enraged gamers who supported AMD and Nvidia for decades and are now feeling left behind as these companies pivoted towards more lucrative AI hardware. title: The original Xbox was released 25 years ago today
summary: Microsoft’s first games console hit North America 25 years ago today powered by a Pentium III CPU and Nvidia GPU.
body: Microsoft’s first games console hit North America 25 years ago today. Effectively a PC in a box, the original Xbox was powered by an Intel Pentium III CPU and an Nvidia GPU inside a bulky black and green case. This first-gen device would sell 24 million units and be succeeded by the sleek PowerPC/ATI-powered Xbox 360 in late 2005. (Image credit: Microsoft) The Xbox arrived on Nov 15, 2001, during the sixth generation of consoles, facing stiff opposition from the legendary Sony PlayStation 2 , Nintendo GameCube, and Sega Dreamcast. However, it established a very respectable foothold in the console market thanks to its formidable hardware and a killer app in the shape of Halo: Combat Evolved . It would end up outselling Nintendo and Sega rivals, only living in the shadow of the PS2. It is interesting to weigh up the performance hardware that was a big reason behind the OG Xbox’s success. Though the contemporary PC parts it used probably made it one of the biggest and ugliest consoles ever, powerful hardware is a great foundation for cutting-edge gaming experiences. title: Wacky PC and gadget gift guide
summary: Our list of fun and wacky PC and gadget gifts is surprising, delightful, and actually useful.
body: The people you want to buy holiday gifts for probably have wishlists, but what happened to surprise and delight? Sometimes, you just have to choose something a bit out of left field to stuff a stocking or fill a gift box and watch as you see your friend or family member's eyes light up. So besides getting your loved ones everything they want, you can also get them a few fun items that surprise and delight. Wacky, even weird, tech that may not be exactly what someone expected to receive, but will certainly make them think of you when they use it. And many of these picks are actually functional. A CD/DVD burner that also happens to be a USB hub, a wireless button to turn your PC on or off, and a clamp-on desk pegboard to keep your workspace neat are just a few of the items you'll find.
